pairs.subject: docs-content-model
pairs.evidence: src/app/guide/page.tsx:12 The /guide landing page is a "use client" component that imports the full GUIDE_TOPICS table and the guide-utils projection functions to compute per-category and total counts in the browser, so the reader downloads the whole record set to render a handful of numbers: the projection that saved nothing.

techniques.evidence: src/app/guide/[category]/[topic]/page.tsx:41 The body-loader map is derived from the category table (lines 46-52), so a missing category content module becomes a resolution failure instead of a report finding. This is the 'make the assertion unnecessary' shape. The route also 404s when the body key is absent (line 95).

src/app/guide/page.tsx:12 Counts are derived and use the visibility predicate (layout.tsx:11 uses countVisibleTopics, so the stale earlier verdict is fixed). But the client page imports the catalog and projection functions instead of receiving projected values. CategoryTopics (a client component) also gets untrimmed GuideTopic records, including coverage metadata, via [category]/page.tsx:136. The boundary is drawn at the function, not the value.

src/app/guide/[category]/[topic]/page.tsx:91 Direct address resolution is gated. Prev/next is built from the filtered collection before indexing (lines 99-104). Category listings and counts filter with isTopicVisible ([category]/page.tsx:21,38). Audience (mode) is a separate predicate used only for listing in page.tsx:25-29; the route never consults it.

src/app/guide/[category]/[topic]/TopicHeader.tsx:27 The product location renders from a typed map keyed by the topic's minted id rather than from prose. The map and its desktop source-of-truth header live in the data context (desktop-modules.ts).

pairs.subject: docs-content-model
pairs.evidence: src/data/guide/topics-nav.ts:45 The navigation projection groups by category but never sorts by a declared position. Neither GuideCategory nor GuideTopic has an order field, so sidebar, category-list and prev/next order all depend on source-declaration order in categories.ts and topics.ts, which the technique names as the one field that must not be implicit.

techniques.evidence: src/data/guide/topics-nav.ts:45 Projection is derived, visibility-filtered and documented as server-only (header at lines 7-23), which is good. But ordering is implicit array order with no declared position and no stable tie-break key.

src/data/guide/content/index.ts:13 The body map is a spread-merge of the per-category modules, so a key present in two category files is silently last-wins. The standalone check's orphan test (scripts/check-guide-content.mjs:103) compares against the global topic-id set, so a stray duplicate body in the wrong category is never flagged. Body-side id uniqueness is unasserted, and /guide-md and llms-full can serve different prose than the topic page. The load tier (guide-utils.ts:87) asserts the category FK only; it does not check topic-id uniqueness.

src/data/guide/topics.ts:3 isTopicVisible (guide-utils.ts:36) is one build-time predicate, and guide-search, sitemap and nav use it. But the short, default accessor every consumer imports is the unfiltered table, so gating relies on discipline. A missed consumer exists: [topic]/opengraph-image.tsx:11 resolves a devOnly topic's title and description, and [category]/opengraph-image.tsx:12 counts drafts. isCategoryVisibleForMode (guide-utils.ts:22) also ignores readiness.

src/data/guide/types.ts:60 Review date, checked-against version and coarse watched sources are typed optional fields. Backfilled dates are spelled differently from earned ones and are never counted as reviewed. Missing watchedFiles or a missing review date is declared to be a named skip class, never drift-free. The coarse watch set is documented as deliberate.

src/data/guide/desktop-modules.ts:5 The cross-artifact mirror names the desktop files that own the vocabulary (lines 5-10) and is the single map keyed by topic id. moduleId is a plain string rather than a compile-time enum; desktop-modules.test.ts guards it instead.
